payload.title: Hybrid Attention Models as First-Class Citizens in vLLM
payload.summary: This document covers the integration of hybrid attention models (combining standard attention with Mamba/linear attention) into vLLM V1, including the unified allocator design, stride alignment, CUDA Graph optimization, and benchmark results.

sections.heading: 1. The Fundamental Bottlenecks of Attention
sections.gist: KV cache memory consumption grows linearly with sequence length, and prefill latency scales quadratically with prompt length.

sections.heading: 2. Why Long Sequences Matter
sections.gist: - **RAG**: User queries concatenated with multiple documents push prompts from thousands to hundreds of thousands of tokens.

sections.heading: 3. A Brief History of SSMs
sections.gist: - **S4 (2021)**: A recurrent structure that maps length-T input sequences to outputs through a latent state h.

sections.heading: 4. V1 Landscape
sections.gist: V1 currently supports hybrid attention models including Nemotron Nano 2, Granite 4.0, Qwen3-Next, MiniMax-Text-01, and Kimi Linear.

sections.heading: 5. State Management: Merging Two Worlds
sections.gist: - **Attention KV cache**: 16-token blocks, approximately 64 KiB per block.

sections.heading: 6. V0: The Fragile Patch
sections.gist: Mamba states were allocated separately, with size guessed from `max_num_seqs`: too high causes OOM, too low reduces concurrency.

sections.heading: 7. V1: The Unified Allocator
sections.gist: The unified allocator manages both KV cache and Mamba state simultaneously.

sections.heading: 8. Stride Adjustment: Perfect Alignment Details

sections.heading: 9. Performance Engineering
sections.gist: **Triton launch overhead** (triton#2637): Significant impact on ITL for small batches and models with few active parameters.

sections.heading: 11. Conclusion
sections.gist: Hybrid attention models in V1 benefit from unified memory allocation, CUDA Graph optimization, prefix caching, KV migration, and PD disaggregation.
